---
title: "Migrate existing METIS work"
---

The original four model families, mathematical explanations and scientific
scope remain the foundation. Current Python, Hydra, distributed execution,
conditioning and resume use the installed `metis` package. Root-level training,
data-loading and model compatibility modules are no longer the active interface.

## Map configurations deliberately

| Earlier source workflow | Installed workflow |
|---|---|
| Root training script and `configs/train` | `uv run metis train` or `Surrogate.fit` |
| `model=mlp_default` | `model=mlp`; set architecture options explicitly when reproducing an old experiment |
| `model.hidden_dim` | `model.model_options.hidden_dim` |
| `model.sit.embd_dim` | `model.model_options.embd_dim` for `model=flow_matching` |
| `dataset.surrogate_input_variables` | `dataset.inputs` |
| `dataset.output_variables` | `dataset.outputs` |
| `dataset.grouping_variables` | `dataset.groups` |
| Hand-entered `num_timesteps` | Inferred and validated from the bank's complete time grid |
| `max_steps`, `peak_lr`, `lr_warmup_frac` | `training.steps`, `training.learning_rate`, `training.warmup_fraction` |
| Original warm-up/cosine schedule | Select `training.schedule=warmup_cosine`; package default is constant |
| `precision`, `deterministic`, `num_gpus` | `training.precision`, `training.deterministic`, `training.num_devices` |
| `logger.use_wandb` | `wandb.enabled` |
| `checkpointer.save_every`, `resume_from` | `training.checkpoint_every`, `training.resume_from`, plus `training.checkpoint_dir` |
| Observed-output configuration | `model.observed_outputs=[name]`; see sequence conditioning |
| Plot-only sample generation | `predict` / `sample` return original-unit arrays; evaluation plotting is optional |

Installed presets are deliberately small enough for a first CPU run. They are
not numerically equivalent to the old small/default/large presets. Set the
architecture, optimizer betas, schedule, precision and split explicitly when
comparing methods. Data validation and train-only scaling also change behavior.
Explicit preprocessing now uses `metis.preprocessing.truncate_simulations` and
`initialize_static_inputs`; these preserve group identity and do not silently
rebase time. See [data preparation](data.qmd).
The corrected final Heun integration step changes generated samples, while its
flow-matching fitting objective is unchanged.

## Preserve the meaning of old checkpoints

An upstream raw checkpoint did not store its normalization statistics. Upstream
computed statistics on the full bank, whereas the current implementation uses
training data only. Applying current preprocessing to old weights can therefore
change predictions even if the original bank and parameters are unchanged.
Preserving the bank alone is insufficient: preserve the exact old code,
configuration, split and preprocessing as well.

Current inference artifacts and resumable training checkpoints have explicit
formats. They reject historical raw checkpoints; do not rename a file to bypass
a format check. A legacy-to-current conversion needs an explicitly reviewed
reconstruction of the original scaling and parity checks on predictions.
A strict importer is available for supported static, float32 models; it does not
guess missing statistics, silently select a historical normalization policy, or
resume the old optimizer.

### Explicit historical import

```python
from metis.migration import LegacyPreprocessing, import_legacy_checkpoint

preprocessing = LegacyPreprocessing.from_dataset(
    exact_full_normalization_bank,
    policy="upstream-full-bank",
    training_data=exact_training_cohort,
    provenance="Original source revision, data version, split and preprocessing record",
)
model = import_legacy_checkpoint(
    "old-checkpoint.pt", preprocessing=preprocessing,
    output_path="imported-inference.pt",
)
```

For the corrected compatibility workflow, select `policy="corrected-training-only"`
and pass the exact training cohort as the first argument instead. If you have
saved means/standard deviations, `LegacyPreprocessing.from_statistics(...)`
accepts them with ordered names, times, known training bounds and provenance.
Its default historical layout is channel/time; `layout="time_channel"` accepts
time/channel output statistics. Historical arithmetic uses float32 and sample
standard deviation, unlike new-fit population statistics. Exact values matter.

The importer accepts only allowlisted architectures with resolved plain
configuration and matching float32 tensor weights. It rejects sequence-conditioned
checkpoints, unsupported/ambiguous architecture settings, unsafe pickled objects,
invalid scales and schema mismatches. There is no unsafe deserialization fallback.
It preserves the original file and records its hash and preprocessing policy in
the new inference artifact. Compare predictions with the trusted original
environment before scientific use; sampling solver corrections can still change
flow-matching output even with the same weights. No old training history, best
step or optimizer state is invented.

For archival reproduction, consult the immutable
[original upstream revision](https://github.com/mrc-ide/metis/tree/c6361c1da68b576c6f24ed2da2387f2792f3a2a8)
or the [last compatibility snapshot](https://github.com/OJWatson/metis/tree/739d57cdaa5f74b9a0973c527f063eaa3a72ab06).
These are historical references, not current installation instructions.

## Two current artifact types

`Surrogate.save` produces an inference bundle for prediction without the bank.
Training checkpoints preserve optimizer/random state for continuation of the
same interrupted experiment. `steps` remains the original total when resuming;
changing the model, data or learning schedule is a new experiment. See
[save and resume](../basics/saving-and-loading.qmd).
